ROUTE_OPTIONS.missing: No legal or route input states what a Penal Code 1203.42-only packet marks in the ten per-conviction 'Eligible for reduction to misdemeanor under Penal Code, section 17(b) (yes or no)' and 'section 17(d)(2) (yes or no)' cells (CR-180 ConvTable rows 1-5). The route record (CA_ROUTE_VARIANTS['ca-1203-42-set']) binds no text controls for them; only the ca-17b-reduction route determines values for row 1. The contract classifies any blank on these labels ROUTE_OPTION_NOT_SELECTED unconditionally, so the only repair is a determined per-route value written into the bytes, which needs a route-record decision (legal input) plus a host mapping plus a re-render. Writing yes/no without that input would be an invented legal determination, the worst possible output. FIX03 reached the same wall from a container without the corpus; this container HAS the corpus and the wall is unchanged, because the block is legal-input and host-mapping, not source availability.

REPEATING_ROWS.missing: incompleteRows=1 is the single pseudo-row 'table::[0]': every XFA terminal name ending in [0] across CR-180, CR-181 and CR-106 collapses into one row (rowKeyOf in the shared completeness contract), and that row holds ~45 REQUIRED_KNOWN-labelled blanks. Zeroing it requires, among others: the petitioner's caption street address/phone/email and the court's street and mailing address (CA_PRIMARY_WRITES binds none; the court address is not a held fact and inventing it is worse than the defect), ink on CR-181 order-body and caption cells and CR-106 service cells describing service that has not occurred, and ink on unchanged-official companion components whose byte-identity to the corpus index is exactly what the ARTIFACTS obligation verifies. This needs host mappings, held facts that do not exist, and a contract-level decision about document-scoped row keys; none of that is repairable from a family directory.
